history.event: Claude refinement: 41 line(s) suggested — Corrected heavily garbled words from the deed and dowry formulae (p̃gio, larghi, sopradecto, monete, rogata, scriptura, aꝑtinentie, deledote, restituire), ꝓ misread for ꝑ (per/parte), the con-sign read as ad/2/an, the monna sign m̄ª, the dates (1493, not 1403/1497), and the figures in the sums (fiorini Cēto, ƒ 9). | layout: l1/l2: the heading ·1493· is split into two tiny boxes covering only '1' and '3'; it should be one line box '·1493·'.; l10/l11: a lone 'di'-like sign between the two boxes is outside both boxes.; l20: the opening 'E' of 'Et' sits partly outside the left edge of the box.; l26: the box joins the marginal note (deladota del mōte …, continued in l27) with the main-text line (del p̃gio … di grossi). They should be separate lines.; l34: between l33 and l35 a whole main-text line (roughly 'epagai fra gabelle e sensale di decta … ') has no box; l34 covers only its final sum 'ƒl. 9.'. Kraken's '69' was this sum.; l35: text struck through after 'decti ƒ' (Cento att. 4), encoded as [del: ]; check how far the strike runs. | doubts: l4, l6–l9, l39: the looped sign before marietta/lisabetta is read as m̄ª (monna); confirm the glyph and the encoding.; l13–l17, l19: the large a/d-shaped sign is read as ꝯ (con: 'con gli eredi', 'con chase', 'con tucti suoi aꝑtinentie') from the sense of the text; confirm.; l10–l11: notary's surname, the 'nore ƒle' abbreviation and the date '148. o…' are unclear; left as Kraken read them.; l33/l35–l36: the figure in l33 could be 57 or 53. 53 + 9 (l34) = 62 = 'sessanta due' (l35–36), so 53 was kept; the ß before 'sessanta' may belong to the deletion.; l21: ebbi or ebbe; l22: iacopo is a guess for the father's name; l24: delugno/notaio uncertain; l28: the names nicholo ghacetti are uncertain.; l25: the day is read as xxvij (the deed in l43 is dated 27 di febraio); Kraken's 'pordoiiº' was garbage, so this is not a change to a roman numeral.; l28, l33–l35: the scribe writes ƒl (florin sign plus a stroke); kept as ƒ as Kraken has it, so check against the MS 1435 conventions.; General: the scribe writes final j (fiorinj, nerj); kept Kraken's i throughout because the MS 1435 j rule is still open.
